title_en: The Story of Little New Year
full_text_zh:
[P1] 小年的故事
连环画出版社

[P2] 从前，有一个皇帝，嘴馋极了，走到哪儿，吃到哪儿，只要没吃过的都要尝尝。

[P4] 这一天，他闲逛到村子里，遇见了一个漂亮姑娘。姑娘提着个篮子。“装的什么呀？”皇帝好奇地问。

[P5] 姑娘打开篮子，哇，好大的枣糕呀！

[P6] 皇帝吃过很多好东西，可就没吃过枣糕。他对姑娘说：
“给我吃点儿吧，我是皇帝！”

[P7] 姑娘微微一笑，把篮子递了过去。

[P8] 皇帝狼吞虎咽，三口五口
就把枣糕吃光了。吃完后打了个嗝儿：“啊呃，真好吃！”

[P9] 接着，皇帝打起了坏主意：“我要把这姑娘带回
皇宫，让她天天给我做枣糕吃！”

[P10] 他对姑娘说：“你马上再给我做七七四十九块枣糕。做不出来，我就把你带走！”

[P11] 姑娘听了，不慌不忙地说：“好！”

[P12] 她拔下头上的金簪，冲着篮子一划。咦？热气腾腾，不多不少，正好七七四十九块枣糕。太神奇了！

[P13] 皇帝还没明白过来。他见难不住姑娘，就耍赖让姑娘喂他吃。
姑娘转过脸去不搭理他！

[P14] 皇帝生气了，非要把姑娘带走。他伸手一抓……

[P15] 姑娘伸出手，一巴掌把皇帝打上了灶台，皇帝一下子贴到了墙头上。

[P16] 这下坏了：皇帝想下来，可怎么也下不来。这一天，刚好是农历的腊月二十三。

[P17] “谁让你嘴馋！这回呀，别人坐着你站着，别人吃着你看着吧！”说完，姑娘驾起彩云飞上天去。贪吃的皇帝从此成了灶王爷。

[P18] 从此以后，
灶王爷就天天站在灶台边，看人家吃饭。

[P19] 时间长了，人们觉得灶王爷怪可怜的——毕竟爱吃好东西也没什么错呀。于是，每到腊月二十三这天，大家就给灶王爷摆上好吃的，这叫做“祭灶”。

[P20] 到了这一天，孩子们最高兴了，他们跟灶王爷一起吃枣糕、柿饼、核桃、糖饼，还有糖瓜。据说，过了腊月二十三，灶王爷就要上天去跟玉皇大帝说说这一年來人间发生的事。他吃了糖瓜嘴巴甜，见了玉皇大帝，就只说人们的好话。

[P22] 腊八过了就是小年，小年在北方是腊月二十三，南方是腊月二十四。从小年开始，就进入了过大年的倒计时。河北邯郸有民谣说：
“糖瓜祭灶二十三，离过年整八天；二十四，扫房子；二十五，做豆腐；二十六，蒸馒头；二十七，赶集上店买东西；二十八，把猪杀；二十九，做黄酒；三十，家家捏饺子。”
小年是要跟灶王爷套近乎的时候。宋代东京（今天的开封）在灶上贴灶马，用酒糟涂抹灶门，这叫“醉司命”。想让灶王爷醉醺醺地上天，糊糊涂涂地交差，别打老百姓的小报告。但是，老让灶王爷醉着也不合适，所以人们用麦芽糖祭灶。用糖粘住灶王爷的嘴巴，让灶王爷嘴巴变甜，上天多说好话。
祭灶用的糖瓜，是用麦芽糖做的。大麦发芽后，上锅熬成浆，冷却后就成了饴糖。邓云乡老爷爷在《增补燕京乡土记》中对糖瓜加工说得很

[P23] 详细：“麦芽糖刚刚熬成时，是咖啡色的浓浆，从锅中盛出来，倒在撒满面粉的石板上，冷却以后变成一大块。做糖瓜时，把这一大块麦芽糖敲下一块，放在撒了干粉的案板上加热揉搓，最后软得像嚼过的口香糖一样。随后把它弄成一个圈，套在一个抹了油的木桩上，再用一个小木棍套上来拉，拉长了再折一转，绞成麻花状再拉，反复多次，说也奇怪，褐色就变成白色的了。拉到这种程度，就可以取下来，把粗长的糖条，用手一段段勒细，成葫芦腰状，稍冷，把细腰处快刀切断，变成倭瓜一样的糖瓜了，多好玩呢？”除了糖瓜，山东人祭灶的时候，也有供饺子的，由此可见山东人对饺子的喜爱。
要是灶王爷不吃这些，老百姓也有办法让他上了天庭不说坏话。据说灶王爷平时要记人间过错，屋里的灰尘是他的笔记本，所以老百姓就在祭灶这天扫屋子，赶灰尘，让灶王爷无话可说。
full_text_en:
[P1] The Story of Xiao Nian
Lian Huan Hua Publishing House

[P2] Once upon a time, there was an emperor who was extremely greedy for food. Wherever he went, he ate whatever he could find, and he had to try anything he had never tasted before.

[P4] One day, he wandered into a village and met a beautiful girl. The girl was carrying a basket. "What's in it?" the emperor asked curiously.

[P5] The girl opened the basket, wow, what a big jujube cake!

[P6] The emperor had eaten many delicious things, but he had never tasted jujube cake. He said to the girl: 
"Give me a little to eat, I'm the emperor!"

[P7] The girl smiled gently and handed over the basket.

[P8] The emperor ate greedily, finishing the jujube cake in three or five bites. After eating, he let out a burp: "Ah, so delicious!"

[P9] Then, the emperor had a bad idea: “I’m going to take this girl back to the palace and have her make jujube cakes for me every day!”

[P10] He said to the girl, "Make me seventy-seven forty-nine more jujube cakes right away. If you can't, I'll take you away!"

[P11] The girl listened, and calmly said: "Okay!"

[P12] She pulled out the golden hairpin from her head and drew a line over the basket. Huh? Steam rising, not too many, not too few—exactly seventy-seven forty-nine jujube cakes. How magical!

[P13] The emperor still hadn't figured it out. Seeing that he couldn't get the girl to give in, he started to act stubborn and asked her to feed him.
The girl turned her face away and ignored him!

[P14] The emperor got angry and insisted on taking the girl away. He reached out to grab her...

[P15] The girl reached out and slapped the emperor onto the stove; he instantly stuck to the wall.

[P16] Oh no: the emperor wanted to come down, but couldn't. This day happened to be the 23rd of the 12th lunar month.

[P17] "Who let you be greedy! This time, while others sit, you stand; while others eat, you watch!" After saying this, the girl rode on a rainbow cloud and flew up to heaven. The greedy emperor thus became the God of the Kitchen.

[P18] From then on,
Zao Wangye stood by the stove every day, watching people eat.

[P19] Over time, people felt sorry for the Kitchen God — after all, loving good food isn’t really wrong. So, every year on the 23rd day of the 12th lunar month, everyone places delicious food before the Kitchen God. This is called 'Ji Zao' (worshipping the Kitchen God).

[P20] On this day, children are the happiest, as they eat jujube cakes, persimmon cakes, walnuts, sugar cakes, and candy melons together with the Kitchen God. It is said that after the 23rd day of the 12th lunar month, the Kitchen God will go up to heaven to report to the Jade Emperor about what has happened in the human world this year. After eating the candy melons, his mouth becomes sweet, and when he meets the Jade Emperor, he only says good things about people.

[P22] After Laba comes Xiao Nian (Little New Year). In the north, Xiao Nian is on the 23rd of the 12th lunar month; in the south, it's on the 24th. From Xiao Nian, the countdown to the Spring Festival begins. There's a folk rhyme from Handan, Hebei: 
"Sugar cakes for the Kitchen God on the 23rd, eight days till New Year; the 24th, clean the house; the 25th, make tofu; the 26th, steam buns; the 27th, go to market to buy things; the 28th, slaughter the pig; the 29th, make yellow wine; the 30th, every family makes dumplings."
Xiao Nian is the time to get close to the Kitchen God. In the Song Dynasty, in Dongjing (today's Kaifeng), people pasted 'Zao Ma' (Kitchen God's horse) on the stove and smeared the stove door with wine lees, called 'Zui Siming' (Drunk Official). They wanted the Kitchen God to be drunk and muddled when he went to heaven, so he wouldn't report on the common people. But keeping the Kitchen God drunk all the time wasn't right, so people used malt sugar to worship him. They used sugar to stick the Kitchen God's mouth, making his mouth sweet so he would say good things when he went to heaven.
The sugar cakes used for worship are made from malt sugar. After barley sprouts, it's boiled into a paste and cooled to become malt syrup. Grandfather Deng Yunxiang described the sugar cake making process very well in his book 'Zengbu Yanjing Tangxiang Ji'.

[P23] Details: "When malt sugar is just boiled, it's a thick, coffee-colored syrup. It's poured onto a stone slab dusted with flour, and after cooling, it becomes a big block. To make sugar gourd, take a piece from this big block of malt sugar, place it on a board dusted with dry flour, heat and knead it until it becomes soft like chewed bubble gum. Then shape it into a ring, put it over an oiled wooden post, and use a small wooden stick to pull it. Pull it long, then fold and twist it, twist it into a braided shape, and pull again. Repeat this many times. Strangely, the brown color turns white. When it reaches this stage, you can take it off, take the long, thick sugar strip, and use your hands to pinch it into sections, forming a gourd-like shape. After it cools slightly, cut it quickly at the narrow waist, turning it into a sugar gourd shaped like a winter melon. How fun!" Besides sugar gourds, when Shandong people worship the Kitchen God, they also offer dumplings, showing how much Shandong people love dumplings.
If the Kitchen God doesn't eat these, the common people also have a way to make sure he doesn't say bad things when he goes to Heaven. It's said that the Kitchen God usually records people's mistakes, and the dust in the house is his notebook. So, the common people sweep the house and remove the dust on the day of worshipping the Kitchen God, so the Kitchen God has nothing to say.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《小年的故事》，由连环画出版社出版。画面以红色为背景，左侧是一位穿着传统服饰的女性形象，右侧是带有年画、帽子、酒壶等物品的供桌，整体风格具有浓厚的中国传统年节特色。
[P2] 本页描绘了一位皇帝在宫殿中用餐的场景，周围有侍女端上食物，下方文字讲述了皇帝嘴馋、什么都想尝一尝的故事开端。
[P3] 画面描绘了一位身穿华丽服饰的皇帝骑在马上，正经过一座传统牌坊，旁边一位挑担的小贩向他递上食物，空中有几只小鸟飞过，场景充满古风市井气息。
[P4] 皇帝在村子里闲逛时，遇见一位提着篮子的漂亮姑娘，好奇地询问篮子里装的是什么。
[P5] 姑娘打开篮子，发现里面装着一个很大的枣糕，显得十分惊喜。
[P6] 皇帝看到姑娘的枣糕后，表示自己从未吃过，便向姑娘索要，并自称是皇帝。
[P7] 姑娘微笑着将装有枣糕的篮子递给了皇帝，画面中可见供桌、炊具和一只小猫，场景温馨而富有年节气息。
[P8] 皇帝狼吞虎咽地吃完了姑娘给的枣糕，吃完后打了个嗝，称赞味道真好。
[P9] 皇帝在吃掉姑娘做的枣糕后，心生贪念，决定将姑娘带回皇宫，让她天天为自己做枣糕。
[P10] 皇帝对姑娘提出要求，让她立即再做七七四十九块枣糕，否则就将她带走。
[P11] 姑娘听到皇帝的要求后，不慌不忙地答应了他，画面中她手持茶壶，身旁有小猫和传统窗格装饰，氛围平静而从容。
[P12] 姑娘用金簪在篮子上一划，瞬间变出七七四十九块热气腾腾的枣糕，皇帝惊叹于这神奇的本事。
[P13] 皇帝想让姑娘喂他吃枣糕，但姑娘转身不理他，表现出拒绝的态度。
[P14] 皇帝因姑娘拒绝喂他吃枣糕而生气，执意要将她带走，并伸手去抓她。
[P15] 姑娘出手反击，一巴掌将皇帝打到灶台上，皇帝被贴在了墙头。
[P16] 皇帝被贴在墙上无法下来，而当天正好是农历腊月二十三，画面中可见灶台、年画和小猫，营造出传统节日氛围。
[P17] 姑娘对皇帝说他贪吃，让他站着看着别人吃，随后驾彩云飞走，贪吃的皇帝则变成了灶王爷。
[P18] 画面描绘了灶王爷站在灶台边，看着一家人准备和享用饭菜的温馨场景，呼应前文他因贪吃被贴在墙上的结局。
[P19] 本页解释了人们为何在腊月二十三祭拜灶王爷，因他贪吃被贴在墙上，人们觉得他可怜，便每年这一天为他摆上美食，称为“祭灶”。画面描绘了灶王爷画像、供品和传统装饰，营造出节日祭拜的温馨氛围。
[P20] 本页描绘了孩子们与灶王爷一起享用祭灶食物的欢乐场景，并解释了人们在腊月二十三给灶王爷吃糖瓜的习俗，是为了让他上天后只说好话。
[P21] 画面描绘了灶王爷驾云来到南天门，两侧有门神守护，上方牌匾写着“南天门”，整体呈现传统神话场景，呼应前文灶王爷上天汇报的结局。
[P22] 本页介绍了小年的习俗，解释了北方腊月二十三、南方腊月二十四过小年的传统，并引用民谣说明了从腊月二十三到除夕的准备活动。同时，详细讲述了祭灶时用糖瓜粘住灶王爷嘴巴的由来，以及糖瓜的制作方法。
[P23] 本页详细介绍了糖瓜的制作过程，并解释了山东人祭灶时供饺子的习俗，同时说明了人们在祭灶日扫尘的由来，即为了让灶王爷无话可说，从而在上天汇报时只说好话。
